sources.source: Children accommodated in secure children's homes: 31 March 2026
sources.verified_fact: The accredited release reports 14 secure children's homes with 218 approved places, 139 children accommodated and a 64% occupancy rate on 31 March 2026. Of those children, 49% were placed on welfare grounds, 45% were placed by the Youth Custody Service and 6% were placed by local authorities in a criminal justice context.
sources.quality_effect: Adds secure-estate capacity context while retaining snapshot-date, approved-versus-available-place, suitability, placement-route and small-cohort fluctuation guards; occupancy is not unmet demand or local safety risk.

sources.verified_fact: The 23 July 2026 updated release reports 357 notifications in the year to 31 March 2026, including 160 relating to child death and 188 relating to serious harm. DfE states that some qualifying incidents may not be notified and proposes ceasing the series because the data is incomplete and not sufficiently reliable for meaningful decision-making.
sources.quality_effect: Adds safeguarding notification context with notification-date, incident-versus-child, incomplete-coverage, reporting-practice and series-cessation guards; the figures cannot be interpreted as incident prevalence or a local risk trend.

sources.source: HM Prison and Probation Service workforce quarterly: March 2026
sources.authority: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.verified_fact: The official release reports an overall HMPPS leaving rate of 9.1% in the year to 31 March 2026 and an average 12.4 working days lost to sickness absence. Mental ill health accounted for 42.9% of working days lost.
sources.quality_effect: Adds operational-capacity context while retaining headcount-versus-FTE, grade, joiner/leaver, organisational-boundary, absence-category and non-causal guards; workforce measures are not prison safety outcomes or parcel indicators.

sources.source: Offender employment outcomes, update to March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The official publication covers employment at six weeks and six months after release or community disposal, with regional and demographic breakdowns. It states that Probation Reset created a break in the time series and that data from May 2024 onwards cannot be compared with data up to April 2024.
sources.quality_effect: Adds rehabilitation-outcome context while retaining eligibility, release-versus-community-disposal, employment-definition, regional-mix and Probation Reset discontinuity guards; these measures are not current offending or local safety rates.

sources.authority: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.verified_fact: The official assessment rated 22 prisons, 18.5% of the estate, as performance of serious concern and 60 prisons, 50.4%, as good or outstanding in 2024/25. Ratings combine 36 measures and are subject to a moderation process.
sources.quality_effect: Adds establishment-performance context while retaining framework-change, measure-weight, target, functional-group and moderation guards; ratings are composite management assessments, not direct incident counts or neighbourhood risk.

sources.source: Asset recovery statistics: financial years ending 2020 to 2025
sources.verified_fact: The official release reports £284.5 million recovered through confiscation, forfeiture and civil recovery orders in the financial year ending March 2025, 15% more than the previous year. It distinguishes receipts from impositions and states that the latest figures supersede earlier official figures.
sources.quality_effect: Adds proceeds-of-crime enforcement context with nominal-versus-real, receipt-versus-order, agency, offence-type, high-value-case and supersession guards; recovered value is not crime prevalence or local enforcement effectiveness.

sources.authority: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.verified_fact: The official UK survey reports that 43% of businesses and 28% of charities identified a cyber breach or attack in the previous 12 months, estimated at about 612,000 businesses and 57,000 charities. The survey warns that unidentified or undisclosed attacks are excluded.
sources.quality_effect: Adds organisational cyber-resilience context with self-identification, willingness-to-report, sampling, organisation-size, breach-versus-cyber-crime and question-wording comparability guards; national organisation estimates are not parcel connectivity risk.

sources.source: Prison Education and Accredited Programme Statistics 2024 to 2025
sources.authority: Ministry of Justice and HM Prison and Probation Service
sources.verified_fact: The official release reports 55,105 prisoners participating in courses and 49,135 achieving in a course in public prisons in England. It also reports 5,456 accredited-programme starts and 4,908 completions in custody in 2024/25.
sources.quality_effect: Adds rehabilitation-input context while retaining participant-versus-enrolment, achievement definition, public-versus-private prison, England-versus-Wales, multiple-course and revised-methodology guards; participation is not proof of reduced reoffending.

sources.verified_fact: The accredited release reports 402,400 children in need at 31 March 2025, a rate of 330.3 per 10,000 children, with returns from all 153 local authorities. The legally defined group includes child-in-need plans, child-protection plans, looked-after children, care leavers and disabled children.
sources.quality_effect: Adds child-social-care demand context while retaining stock-versus-flow, episode-versus-child, legal-definition, referral, assessment and local-recording guards; children-in-need counts are not abuse prevalence or neighbourhood safety scores.

sources.source: Children in need: A focus on sexual abuse and exploitation
sources.verified_fact: The official analytical release reports 29,560 children assessed with child sexual abuse recorded as a factor and 12,120 with child sexual exploitation recorded in the year ending March 2025. It warns that local recording practices vary and that assessment factors must not be treated as prevalence.
sources.quality_effect: Adds safeguarding crosschecks while retaining assessment-factor, multiple-factor, local-practice, reporting-year, child-on-child and police-recorded-crime comparability guards; recorded factors are not measured incidence or parcel risk.

quality_guards: AREA_OR_SYSTEM_LEVEL_CONTEXT only; no parcel measurement claim.
Secure-home counts are annual snapshots of a small cohort and do not establish unmet demand.
Serious incident notification data is incomplete and is held as a reliability warning only.
HMPPS workforce measures do not directly measure prison or community safety outcomes.
Probation Reset creates a time-series break in offender employment outcomes from May 2024.
Prison performance ratings are composite, weighted and moderated assessments.
Asset recovery receipts, impositions and denied assets are distinct financial measures.
Cyber breach survey estimates include only attacks organisations identified and reported.
Prison education participants, enrolments, achievements and programme completions are separate units.
Children-in-need stocks, episodes, referrals and assessments are separate social-care measures.
Child sexual abuse and exploitation assessment factors vary with local recording practice and are not prevalence.
No existing candidate score, endpoint manifest, database row or stored parcel value was modified.
